summary:
Paper (Sah–Sahasrabudhe–Sawhney, arXiv:2405.20308v2). Theorem 1.1 (p.1): for an n x n matrix M with iid subgaussian entries (mean 0, var 1), P(sigma_n(M) <= eps n^{-1/2}) <= (1+o(1)) eps + e^{-Omega_xi(n)} for all eps >= 0, o(1) = C_xi (log n)^{-1/16}. Theorem 1.2 (p.2): P(sigma_n(M) <= eps n^{-1/2}) = (1+o(1)) P(sigma_n(G) <= eps n^{-1/2}) + e^{-Omega(n)} (two-sided, Gaussian G), so the least-singular-value law is universal down to exponentially small scales up to a 1+o(1) factor; Cor. 1.3 is Thm 1.1 with Edelman's bound (Thm 9.4). Working regime e^{-cn} < eps < n^{-c} (Sec. 2, p.4; the rest is Rudelson–Vershynin / Tao–Vu). The proof is: (1) exact 'random geometric normalisation' (Lemma 3.2, secular equation (23)): sigma_n(M) is the root of 1 + sum_i <v_i,X>^2/(sigma_i^2 - x^2) = <v,X>^2/x^2 with v the kernel vector of the first n-1 rows M*, so {sigma_n <= eps n^{-1/2}} is sandwiched between {|<v,X>| <= (1 +- eps^{1/4}) eps n^{-1/2} chi~(X)} (Lemma 3.3, (21)-(22)), chi~^2 = 1 + sum_{i<n} <v_i,X>^2/sigma_i(M*)^2 (eq. 12). VERIFIED numerically (random 50x51 M*, 51x51 M): secular residual 7e-13, lambda = z^2/(1+sum g_i^2/(s_i^2-lambda)) to 1e-14 relative, Lemma 3.2 determinant identity to 1e-13. (2) Truncation (Lemmas 4.1-4.3, Secs 4-7): on a regularity event R the sum is replaced by its ell = sqrt(log n) smallest-singular-direction terms at a factor 1+O(delta_n), delta_n = (log n)^{-c}, and P(rare ∧ R^c) = O(delta_n eps) (Lemma 4.2). (3) Gaussian replacement (Sec. 8, Lemma 8.1): for M* in a quasirandom event E* the last row X is exchanged for Gaussian Z at relative cost O(delta_n eps) (replacement proper: eps n^{-Omega(1)}, Lemma 8.5). (4) Rescaling (Lemma 9.2): the Gaussian small-ball probability is exactly homogeneous in eps, so eps is replaced by eps_0 = n^{-c}, where Tao–Vu's absolute O(n^{-c'}) universality (Thm 9.3) becomes a relative o(eps_0) error; then Edelman. The methodological core: every error is bounded RELATIVE to eps (O(delta_n eps) or eps n^{-Omega(1)}), never absolutely, except e^{-Omega(n)} terms which are allowed only because eps >= e^{-cn}; the smallness eps is an exact multiplicative prefactor (|<v,X>| small along one realisation-specific direction v) of a POSITIVE O(1) geometry chi(X) whose terms decay like 1/i^2 (sigma_{n-i} ~ i n^{-1/2}), and all approximations (truncation, smoothing, replacement) act on the O(1) geometry, needing only (log n)^{-c} relative accuracy. CHECKED on a forced rare event at n=1000: lambda = z^2/chi~^2 to 4e-4 relative at eps=1e-2 (2e-9 at eps=1e-4); ell=3 directions carry 91-94% of chi~^2, ell=10 97%.

Our regime. PROVED (arithmetic from notes/stage9/sec_measure.tex, sec_capacity.tex): the correction e - a delta(0) has residual MSE (1-rho^2) MSE_chain = 6.6e-9 (rho = 0.902, a = rho err/|delta| = 0.257), and an incoherent relative error r on delta adds (r a |delta|)^2: r = 0.1 -> +4%, 0.2 -> +17%, 0.5 -> +108%. So delta (rms 6.6e-4 absolute, 1.6e-3 of |e| ~ 0.4; the task's 7e-4 is the absolute rms) must be known to ~20% of itself = 1.3e-4 absolute = 3e-4 of |e|, the same absolute tolerance class as F4 (3% slices to 1e-2 = 3e-4 of O(1)) and F6 (1e-3 variance -> 4e-4 mean shift). This IS the paper's rare-event-relative regime: tolerances on all O(1) intermediates are set by the size of the small target, so 'small' absolute errors (MC noise 1e-3, compression 1e-2) are fatal while float roundoff (1e-15, the analogue of e^{-Omega(n)}) is harmless; probing Lap e to that accuracy needs S ~ 7e7-3e8 Hutchinson probes (notes: 1e9 for 1e-4), the analogue of Tao–Vu's absolute n^{-c} being useless at scale eps. BUT the structure differs: the paper's smallness is multiplicative (exact prefactor, positive few-direction-dominated geometry); ours is additive (delta = e - Lap e, |Lap e| ~ |e|; the bulk hub pairing is a zero-mean sum of n comparable random-sign terms, F2/F3). CHECKED (new script, Gaussian closure, L=4, n=32/64/96; Gram theorem reproduced to 7e-8): the Gram form delta = -tr Q (Q = Hessian of the chain-from-layer-2 pulled back through the first-layer tangent map, Q_ij = d^2 G along grad_i theta, grad_j theta) is also cancelling: positive eigenvalue mass share 0.38-0.57, sum|lambda|/|tr Q| = 6, 11, 15 (growing with n), top-8 |lambda| share of sum|lambda| 0.79, 0.56, 0.46 (flattening with n), Hutchinson relative noise sqrt2||Q||_F/|tr Q| = 3.7, 4.2, 5.3. Consequences: (i) the paper's few-direction truncation has no analogue for delta (no positivity, flat spectrum) nor for the memory (F2, F3, L1: flat importance profile, 99%-rank > 256, incoherent error); a systematic approximation Q~ with ||Q~-Q||_F <= r||Q||_F can shift tr Q by sqrt(n) r ||Q||_F ~ 100 r |delta| at n=1024, so r ~ 1e-3 would be needed — the Gram form does not relax systematic tolerances. (ii) What does transfer is the eps-prefactor discipline for UNBIASED noise: probing tr Q instead of tr H_y makes the noise relative to delta (4-5/sqrt S, so S ~ 600-2500 for r = 0.2-0.1) instead of relative to e (1e9 probes), a 1e5-1e6 reduction — but each probe costs 2 chain evaluations and S is of the same order as the exact coordinate sum 2n+1 = 2049, so no cost gain; the symbolic second-order response (task #9) remains the only route below O(n) chain runs. (iii) 'Keep the random normalisation' = compute with the realisation's own geometry: the chain already conditions on all weights; the memory's effect is a realisation-specific zero-mean functional (F2), the exact analogue of the kernel vector v (E_{M*} v is meaningless), so no mean-field/ensemble replacement exists for it, and a Gaussian replacement of the law of W_L would annihilate it; the paper's replacement is of an independent component inside a test function of mass eps (Claim C.2), i.e. after the smallness is factored out — the Gaussian closure replaces before (error 2e-3 >> delta), the kappa3 chain is the third-order Lindeberg term (Thm 8.4's structure, delocalised He rows = Lemma 7.5 flatness). (iv) 'Justify errors on the event' translates to the correction floor (1-rho^2) MSE_short for Euler–Stein corrections of short-memory chains: to reach 1e-8 one needs rho >= sqrt(1 - 1e-8/MSE_short) = 0.9987 (MSE 3.7e-6, windows 1-2 dropped), 0.993 (7.4e-7, w=4 dropped), 0.975 (2.0e-7, w=2 rank-4 old), 0.934 (7.8e-8, w=2 rank-64), against measured rho = 0.90-0.91 (exact chain), 0.93-0.95 (Gaussian closure): this is the deciding number for task #13, and it says the Euler–Stein route from a window-1/2 chain needs a qualitatively more correlated defect (possible only if the short chain's 53-64% collective error, F7, is captured by delta with rho ~ 0.999). (v) The rescaling lever (Lemma 9.2) has no analogue: delta is affine, not homogeneous, in the birth amplitude (first-order chain is linear in births), and the one exact homogeneity available (OU semigroup, (1+tau)^{-d/2}) is already used in a = 1/(d+1).

mechanisms.name: M1 Random geometric normalisation (secular/resolvent reduction)
mechanisms.statement: Lemma 3.2 (p.7): for A n x n with last row Y removed giving A* with singular values 0 = sigma_n(A*) <= ... and right singular vectors u_i, det(A^T A - xI) = det(A*^T A* - xI)(1 + Y^T (A*^T A* - xI)^{-1} Y), so the singular values of A solve prod_i(sigma_i(A*)^2 - x)(1 + sum_i <u_i,Y>^2/(sigma_i(A*)^2 - x)) = 0. Eq. (23) (p.7): sigma_n(A) is the unique root in [0, sigma_{n-1}] of 1 + sum_{i<n} <u_i,Y>^2/(sigma_i^2 - x^2) = <u,Y>^2/x^2, u in ker(A*). Lemma 3.3 (p.7): if sigma_{n-1}(A*) >= eps^{3/4} n^{-1/2}, sigma_n(A) <= eps n^{-1/2} implies |<u,Y>| <= (1+eps^{1/4}) eps n^{-1/2} chi~(Y); conversely sigma_n(A) > eps n^{-1/2} implies |<u,Y>| > eps n^{-1/2} chi~(Y) unconditionally; chi~^2(Y) = 1 + sum_{i<n} <u_i,Y>^2/sigma_i(A*)^2 (eq. 12, p.4). Lemma 3.1 (p.7) then gives (11) with error O(delta_n eps) using Thm 3.4 (Rudelson–Vershynin: P(sigma_{n-1}(M*) <= gamma n^{-1/2}) <= C gamma^2 + 2e^{-Omega(n)}). Rudelson–Vershynin's (10) (p.4) loses a constant C because it discards chi~; keeping the full secular correction is what makes the constant 1.
mechanisms.status: PROVED in the paper (matrix determinant lemma + monotonicity of (23)); CHECKED numerically here: random 50x51 M* with kernel vector v, appended row X: secular residual -7e-13, lambda = z^2/(1+sum g_i^2/(s_i^2-lambda)) to 1e-14 relative, bisection root agrees to 6e-15, Lemma 3.2 determinant identity at x=0.3 to 1.2e-13 relative; on a forced rare event (n=1000, <v,X> set so sigma_n = eps n^{-1/2}) lambda = z^2/chi~^2 holds to 4.3e-4 relative at eps = 1e-2 and 2.3e-9 at eps = 1e-4, i.e. the true factor is 1 + O(eps^2) (from (24): 1/(1-(x/sigma_i)^2)), the paper's (1+2eps^{1/4}) being loose to allow sigma_{n-1} ~ eps^{3/4} n^{-1/2}.
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: The smallness (eps) enters as an exact scalar prefactor on one realisation-specific direction v; the O(1) geometry chi~ is a positive sum. Our delta = e - y.grad e - Lap e (F5) and the bulk hub pairing (F2) have no such prefactor form: delta is a difference of O(1) terms (|Lap e(0)| ~ |e| ~ 0.4, sec_capacity.tex), the memory is a zero-mean cubic functional. The Gram theorem delta = -<Hess G, Gamma> (sec_births.tex Thm gram) is the candidate analogue but is CHECKED to be cancelling (M8).

mechanisms.name: M2 Truncation to ell = sqrt(log n) low singular directions on a regularity event
mechanisms.statement: Definitions (14) p.5: delta_n = (log n)^{-c}, ell = sqrt(log n), chi^2(X) = sum_{i<=ell} <v_{n-i},X>^2/sigma_{n-i}(M*)^2. Lemma 4.1 (p.8): for e^{-cn} < eps < n^{-c}, P(sigma_n(M) <= eps n^{-1/2}) <= P(|<v,X>| <= (1+delta_n) eps n^{-1/2} chi(X)) + O(delta_n eps), and conversely with (1-delta_n). Regularity R = R1∩R2∩R3∩R4 (p.9): R1: sigma_{n-1}(M*) >= (log n)^{-3} n^{-1/2}; R2: |<v_{n-k},X>| <= max{k^{1/8}, log log n} for all k and sigma_{n-k}(M*) >= k^{3/4} n^{-1/2} for k >= log log n; R3: sigma_{n-(log log n)^2}(M*) <= (log log n)^3 n^{-1/2}; R4: sum_{i<=(log log n)^2} <v_{n-i},X>^2 >= log log n. Lemma 4.3 (p.9, deterministic): on R, chi~^2 = (1+O(delta_n)) chi^2 because the lower bound (28) gives chi~^2 >= n/(log log n)^5 while the tail sum_{i>ell} <v_{n-i},X>^2/sigma_{n-i}^2 <= n sum_{i>ell} i^{1/4}/i^{3/2} ~ n ell^{-1/4} = n (log n)^{-1/8}. Lemma 4.2 (p.9): P(sigma_n(M) <= eps n^{-1/2} ∧ R^c) = O(delta_n eps), proved in Secs 5-7 (Lemmas 6.1, 7.1).
mechanisms.status: PROVED in the paper (the deterministic part is a positive-series tail bound; the probabilistic part is M3). CHECKED here at finite n: on the forced rare event at n=1000 the ell smallest directions carry 83-93% (ell=1), 91-94% (ell=3 ~ sqrt(log n)), 97% (ell=10), 98-99% (ell=30) of chi~^2; without conditioning on the rare event (typical X, sigma_n not small) the shares are erratic (ell=1: 5%), which is exactly why the truncation is justified only on R.
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: Truncation works because (a) all terms are positive (one-sided error), (b) sigma_{n-i} ~ i n^{-1/2} makes the terms decay like 1/i^2. Neither holds for our objects: the cocycle's 99%-rank exceeds 256 at ages 1-3 (F3), the hub importance profile is flat (F3, L1), the exact chain's error is incoherent (F7), and the Gram-form Hessian has balanced-sign eigenvalues with a flattening spectrum (M8). So F2/F3/F7 are the measured statement that the paper's truncation lever is absent for the memory.

mechanisms.name: M3 Errors on the rare event: product (decoupling) bounds
mechanisms.statement: Lemma 5.1 (p.10): for E measurable w.r.t. M*, 0 < eps <= 1, delta in [eps^{3/4},1]: P(sigma_n(M) <= eps n^{-1/2} ∧ sigma_{n-1}(M*) >= delta n^{-1/2} ∧ E) <~ n (eps/delta) P(E) + e^{-Omega(n)}. Lemma 5.2 (p.10), eq (31): under E_r (|<X,v_{n-k}>| <= max{k^{1/8}, r}, sigma_{n-k}(M*) >= k^{3/4} n^{-1/2} for k >= r) the factor n improves to r^{3/2}. Lemma 5.3 (p.10), eqs (32)-(33): with the non-M*-measurable event {|<w,X>| >= t} the factor becomes e^{-Omega(t^2)} (negative correlation of small-ball and large-deviation events, Thm 5.8 from Campos–Jenssen–Michelen–Sahasrabudhe). Mechanism: Lemma 3.3 turns the rare event into a small-ball event for <v,X> conditional on M* (Lemma 5.4, 5.7), then max_{M* in E ∩ E_lcd} P_X(|<v,X>| <= t | M*) <= C(t + e^{-cn}) by Thm 5.6 (Rudelson–Vershynin small-ball for vectors with LCD >= C/t), with Thm 5.5: P(exists v in ker M* with LCD(v) < e^{cn}) <= 2e^{-cn}. Then dyadic decomposition (Lemmas 6.2, 6.5) sums n eps/gamma_j * gamma_j^2 over scales to eps/n; Thm 6.3 (Nguyen) and Lemma 7.2 (Szarek/Tao–Vu) give the tails of sigma_{n-k}(M*); Thm 7.4 (simpler negative-correlation lemma, Appendix B) and Lemma 7.5 (flatness: P(exists unit v with ||v||_inf > C n^{-c} and ||M* v|| < 1) < n^{-omega(1)}, Appendix A) handle R4.
mechanisms.status: PROVED in the paper (not re-derived here beyond reading the proofs; the decoupling theorems are cited from [4], [17], [21], [26], [27]).
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: The acceptable probability p of a bad event is set by the relative loss p * (small-ball factor n/delta or r^{3/2}/delta), never by p being absolutely small. Translation: in our error budget (M7) an approximation is acceptable iff its contribution to delta is <= 20% of delta, regardless of how small it is relative to e; an exceptional-set accounting over the WEIGHT ensemble (what fraction of networks violate a = 1/(d+1) by more than x) has not been done — the crossover tests on nets 0/1 (a = 0.255 vs 0.257, sec_measure.tex) are two samples. CONJECTURE: the right acceptance test for a derived constant is relative loss on the correction, as in Lemma 5.1.

mechanisms.name: M4 Error taxonomy: exponentially small vs o(eps) vs eps n^{-Omega(1)}
mechanisms.statement: Three classes appear. (A) e^{-Omega(n)}, absolute: LCD failure (Thm 5.5), ||X||^2 >= n log n (proof of Lemma 5.1, p.11), the additive terms of Thms 3.4, 5.6, 5.8, 6.3; admissible only because eps >= e^{-cn} with c small (Sec. 2, p.4) — they never appear inside a bound that must hold at eps = e^{-Cn} for large C. (B) O(delta_n eps) = (log n)^{-c} eps, relative: regularity failure (Lemma 4.2), the (1 +- delta_n) truncation factor (Lemma 4.3), bump smoothing (Claims C.3, C.4, p.27-28: |E f^+(G) - f^-(G)| = O(delta_n eps) and P_X(F) <= E f(H) + O(delta_n eps)), rescaling (Lemma 9.2: (1 +- n^{-c/8}) and the tail sum sum_j eps 2^{j+1} e^{-Omega(4^j/(log n)^{3/2})}). (C) eps n^{-Omega(1)} from the replacement (Lemma 8.5, (55)). The single absolute-error tool, Tao–Vu's universality P(sigma_n(M~) <= eps n^{-1/2}) = P(sigma_n(G) <= eps n^{-1/2}) + O(n^{-c}) (Thm 9.3, p.22), is applied only at scale eps_0 = n^{-c} with c smaller than Tao–Vu's exponent, after the exact rescaling of Lemma 9.2 has blown the quantity up, so that n^{-c'} = o(eps_0) (eq. (20), p.6). The final o(1) = C(log n)^{-1/16} is set by class (B).
mechanisms.where: Sec. 2 p.4-6 (assumptions and outline), Sec. 5.1 p.11, Sec. 8.3 eq. (55) p.19, Sec. 9 Lemmas 9.1-9.3 and eq. (20) p.21-23, Appendix C p.26-28
mechanisms.status: PROVED (reading of the paper; the classification is mine, the bounds are theirs).
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: Analogue of (A): float roundoff 1e-15 on O(1) objects (the kprop3 port matches the reference to 1e-15); harmless. Analogue of (B)/(C): everything that must be relative to delta or to the 3% slice residuals (F4). Analogue of the misuse the paper avoids: a Monte-Carlo or sketch estimate with absolute noise 1e-3 on e (F4: zero-mean Gaussian sketches, 1e4-1e6 samples) is the Tao–Vu n^{-c} used at scale eps — useless; the paper's fix (rescale first) has no analogue for delta (M10).

mechanisms.name: M5 Gaussian replacement at scale o(eps)
mechanisms.statement: Lemma 8.1 (p.17), eqs (49)-(50): for M* in E* and v in ker(M*), P_X(|<v,X>| <= eps n^{-1/2} chi(X)) <= P_Z(|<v,Z>| <= (1+delta_n) eps n^{-1/2} chi(Z)) + O(delta_n eps), and the reverse with (1-delta_n). E* (p.18, eqs (52)-(53)): sigma_{n-1}(M*) >= (log n)^{-3} n^{-1/2}, sigma_{n-k}(M*) >= k^{3/4} n^{-1/2} (k >= log log n), sigma_{n-(log log n)^2}(M*) <= (log log n)^3 n^{-1/2}, sigma_{n-sqrt(log n)}(M*) <= (log n) n^{-1/2}, LCD(v) > e^{cn}, ||v||_inf, ||v_{n-1}||_inf, ..., ||v_{n-ell}||_inf < n^{-Omega(1)}; Lemma 8.2: P(rare ∧ (E*)^c) = O(delta_n eps). Steps: (i) the event depends on X only through H = (<v,X>, <v_{n-1},X>, ..., <v_{n-ell},X>) in R^{ell+1}; (ii) Lemma 8.3 / Appendix C builds bump functions f^+-, f^- = (B_{r +- tau^{-1}} Q C) * rho with Q restricting to |x| <= eps (log n)^5, ||y||_inf <= log n, whose Fourier transforms satisfy |f^(theta, xi)| <= eps exp((log n)^{2/3}) exp(-c (log n)^{-26}(|theta eps|^{1/2} + sum |xi_i|^{1/2})) (Claim C.2) — the prefactor eps is ||Q||_{L^1}, i.e. the mass of the event; (iii) Lemma 8.5, eq. (55): |E_X f(H) - E_K f(K)| <= eps n^{-Omega(1)}, proved by Fourier inversion over Omega = {|theta| <= eps^{-1} (log n)^{28}, ||xi||_inf <= (log n)^{30}}: for |theta| <= (log n)^{30} Theorem 8.4 (Lindeberg: |E f(X) - E f(Z)| <= max E|X_i|^3 sum_i ||d^3 f/dx_i^3||_inf) applied to g(x) = exp(-2 pi i <x, u>), u = theta v + sum xi_i v_i, gives error <= sum u_i^3 <= ||u||_inf ||u||_2^2 <= n^{-Omega(1)} using flatness; for |theta| >= (log n)^{30} both characteristic functions are n^{-omega(1)}: the Gaussian one trivially, the X one by (54) |E exp(i<u,Y>)| <= exp(-c_0 inf_r ||r v||_T^2) with ||theta v||_T >~ min{|theta|, sqrt n} from LCD(v) > e^{cn} (the 'arithmetic quasirandomness'). Then by rotational invariance (16): (<v,Z>, sum <v_i,Z>^2/sigma_i^2) = (W_n, sum W_i^2/sigma_i^2) with iid normals.
mechanisms.where: Sec. 2.3 eqs (15)-(16) p.5; Sec. 8 Lemmas 8.1-8.5, eqs (49)-(59) p.17-21; Appendix C Lemma C.1, Claims C.2-C.4, eqs (69)-(72) p.26-28
mechanisms.status: PROVED in the paper. Not numerically checked here (would require sampling exponentially rare events).
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: The replacement error inherits the eps prefactor from the L^1 mass of the test function and is relative because it is applied to the already-extracted small quantity. Our Gaussian closure replaces the pre-activation law BEFORE the small quantity is extracted (error 2e-3 on means, MSE 4e-6, >> delta = 6.6e-4), the kappa3 chain is the third-order Lindeberg term (Thm 8.4's sum_i u_i^3 structure; delocalisation of He rows w_b.u ~ N(0, 2/n), sec_central.tex Prop. sens, is the analogue of Lemma 7.5 flatness), and its remaining defect delta is the effect of the fourth-and-higher-order remainder plus the first-order transport deficit (F5). The paper's lesson: replacement must act inside a quantity that already carries the small prefactor; for the memory (F2: zero-mean cubic functional of W_L) replacing the law of W_L annihilates the quantity, so no Gaussian/ensemble replacement of the last layer is admissible — only the realisation's value counts, exactly as only the realisation's v counts in the paper.

mechanisms.name: M6 Rescaling by exact homogeneity and return to the singular-value problem
mechanisms.statement: Lemma 9.2 (p.21): for 0 <= eps <= n^{-c}, eps_0 in [n^{-c}, n^{-c/2}], sigma_{n-1}(M*) >= (log n)^{-1} n^{-1/2}: P_Z(|<v,Z>| <= eps n^{-1/2} chi(Z)) = (eps/eps_0) P_Z(|<v,Z>| <= eps_0 n^{-1/2} chi(Z)) + O(delta_n eps). Proof: write the event as |W_0| <= eps f(W_1..W_ell) with W iid N(0,1) and f <= (log n)^{5/4} max|W_i|; on f < n^{c/4} the Gaussian density is (2 pi)^{-1/2}(1 + O(t^2)) so P(|W_0| <= eps f ∧ f < n^{c/4}) = (eps/eps_0)(1 +- n^{-c/8}) P(|W_0| <= eps_0 f ∧ f < n^{c/4}); the tail f >= 2^j is dyadically summed with P(f >= t) <= log n e^{-Omega(t^2/(log n)^3)} (eq. 61). Lemma 9.1 (p.21), eq. (60): E_{M*} P_Z(...) = (1+O(delta_n)) P_G(sigma_n(G) <= eps n^{-1/2}) + O(delta_n eps), by applying Lemma 4.1 in reverse to M~ = (M*; Z), then Thm 9.3 (Tao–Vu) and Thm 9.4 (Edelman: P(sigma_n(G) <= eps n^{-1/2}) <= eps). Proof of Thm 1.2 (p.23) chains Lemma 4.1, Lemma 8.1, Lemma 9.1.
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: This lever needs a parameter in which the small quantity is exactly homogeneous. CONJECTURE (negative, with reason): delta has none — the first-order chain is linear in its kappa3 births, so delta_t for births scaled by t is affine (delta_G + t(delta_1 - delta_G)), and delta_1 is itself a 7% residual of the Gaussian closure's delta_G ~ 1e-2 (sec_capacity.tex: |delta| ~ 1e-2 vs |e| ~ 0.4 for the closure; 6.6e-4 for the kappa3 chain, sec_measure.tex); the one exact homogeneity in play, the OU semigroup's (1+tau)^{-d/2} decay on Eldan's path (P1), is already consumed by a = 1/(d+1) (F5).

mechanisms.name: M7 Our precision budget: delta is rare-event-relative
mechanisms.statement: With err_rms = sqrt(3.53e-8) = 1.88e-4, |delta(0)|_rms = 6.6e-4, rho = corr(delta, err) = 0.902 (net 0; 0.914 net 1), least squares gives a = rho err/|delta| = 0.257 (reported 0.255) and residual MSE (1-rho^2) 3.53e-8 = 6.6e-9 (reported 6.64e-9). An incoherent relative error r on delta adds (r a |delta|)^2: r = 0.05: +1%, 0.1: +4%, 0.2: +17%, 0.3: +39%, 0.5: +108%. Hence delta is needed to ~20% of itself = 1.3e-4 absolute = 3.3e-4 of |e| ~ 0.4 (|delta|/|e| = 1.6e-3; the task's 7e-4 is |delta|_rms itself). Hutchinson on Lap e (relative noise 2.8/sqrt S on tr H ~ 0.4, sec_capacity.tex) needs S = (2.8 * 0.4/(r 6.6e-4))^2 = 7e7 (r = 0.2) to 3e8 (r = 0.1) probes; the notes' 1e9 corresponds to r ~ 0.05. The exact coordinate sum is 2n+1 = 2049 chain runs.

mechanisms.name: M8 Multiplicative vs additive smallness: the Gram form is cancelling (new numerical check)
mechanisms.statement: The Gram theorem (sec_births.tex Thm gram) gives delta(0) = -sum_{AB} d_A d_B G(theta) Gamma_AB = -tr Q with Q_ij = second derivative of G (chain from layer 2 as a function of the first-layer moments (mu, M)) along the tangent directions grad_i theta, grad_j theta of the input coordinates (Gamma = grads grads^T, so <Hess G, Gamma> = sum_i d^2_{grad_i theta} G). Computed Q (n x n per output) by central differences in moment space for He-random Gaussian-closure chains, L = 4, n = 32, 64, 96 (KH = 40 Hermite terms), and the input Hessian H_y of e (tr H_y = Lap e). Results: Gram theorem reproduced (max |delta + tr Q| = 7e-8, 5e-8, 1.5e-7 vs |delta|_rms = 6.3e-2, 3.1e-2, 2.6e-2; |delta|/|e| = 6.3e-2, 5.2e-2, 3.2e-2 falling with n toward the 2.5e-2 of n = 1024). Spectrum of Q: positive eigenvalue mass share 0.38-0.57 per output (balanced signs); mean sum|lambda| / mean |tr Q| = 6.2, 11.5, 15.0; median Hutchinson relative noise sqrt2 ||Q||_F/|tr Q| = 3.7, 4.2, 5.3; mean |lambda| profile (share of sum|lambda|) top-1: 0.25, 0.15, 0.13; cumulative top-8: 0.79, 0.56, 0.46 — flattening with n; the top-1/3/8 eigenvalue shares of tr Q itself are erratic (+2.5, -4.5, -51 for individual outputs). For H_y the ratio sqrt2 ||H||_F/|tr H| is 0.5-6 per output (notes: ~2 at n = 1024).

mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: (i) The paper's truncation lever requires positive terms with 1/i^2 decay; Q has balanced signs and a flattening spectrum, so truncating delta to few directions is not controlled (consistent with the report's k-direction tilt SNR sqrt(k) 1e-2 and the sign-changing S = 16 probe fits). (ii) A systematic approximation Q~ with ||Q~ - Q||_F <= r ||Q||_F can shift tr Q by up to sqrt(n) r ||Q||_F ~ 100 r |delta| at n = 1024 — the Gram form does NOT relax systematic tolerances (low-rank, compressed, mean-field Q are all uncontrolled), which is the F2/F3 Hadamard obstruction seen from the second-order side (sec_births.tex remark 3: E[delta S_ab^2] is O(n^4)). (iii) What the Gram form does deliver is the paper's eps-prefactor discipline for UNBIASED noise: Hutchinson on tr Q has noise relative to delta (4-5/sqrt S) instead of relative to e (2.8 |e|/|delta| ~ 1700/sqrt S at n = 1024): S ~ 600 (r = 0.2) to 2500 (r = 0.1) probes of 2 chain-from-layer-2 evaluations each, vs 1e8-1e9 probes on Lap e — a 1e5 reduction, but of the same order as the exact 2n+1 = 2049 coordinate sum and with a ratio growing slowly with n, so no cost gain over the exact sum; the symbolic O(n^3)-per-layer second-order response (task #9) remains the only route below O(n) chain runs.

mechanisms.name: M9 'Keep the random normalisation' for the memory's effect
mechanisms.statement: In the paper nothing is ever averaged over M*: v, v_i, sigma_i are the realisation's own; E* is a typicality event, not an ensemble average; the one component whose law is replaced (X -> Z) is independent of the geometry and enters only through its projections on (v, v_{n-1}..v_{n-ell}) (Sec. 8.2, p.18). The bulk hub pairing (F2) is cubic in the last weight matrix with zero ensemble mean — the analogue of v: realisation-specific, mean zero over the ensemble (E_{M*} v is not a meaningful object either). F2's measurement (coherent + cross + diagonal parts recover nothing: 1.65e-6 -> 1.2e-6; star + residual bulk recover everything: 3.5e-8) is the statement that the memory's effect has no mean-field surrogate.
mechanisms.where: paper Sec. 8.1-8.2 p.18, Sec. 2.3 p.5; our_problem.md F2, F7; REPORT.md Sec. 2 (two-tier diagnostics)
mechanisms.status: PROVED for the paper's side (reading); CHECKED on our side by the existing F2 experiments; the correspondence itself is an analogy (CONJECTURE as a guide, not a theorem).
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: Concretely: (a) no ensemble/Gaussian replacement of W_L or of the old sources' statistics can reproduce the memory's effect (F3 'not regenerable from current statistics' is the same fact); (b) the chain's conditioning on all weights, with the input x as the only randomness, is the correct analogue of fixing M*; (c) the only admissible replacement is of an independent component inside the small quantity — the input law along Eldan's path (F5), which is what the Euler–Stein correction already does. The route the paper suggests is therefore not a cheaper memory but a correction of the memory's EFFECT computed with the realisation's own cocycle (the Gram/second-order object of P3), subject to the floor in M10.

mechanisms.name: M10 Floor of Euler–Stein corrections of short-memory chains (the deciding number for task #13)
mechanisms.statement: For any chain with error E and defect delta, the best correction e - a delta has MSE (1-rho^2) MSE_chain + (fitting/precision terms). To reach 1e-8 from a short-memory chain one needs rho >= sqrt(1 - 1e-8/MSE_short): MSE 3.7e-6 (windows 1-2 dropped): rho >= 0.9987; 7.4e-7 (w = 4 dropped): 0.9932; 2.0e-7 (w = 2, rank-4 old): 0.975; 7.8e-8 (w = 2, rank-64 old): 0.934; 3.5e-8 (exact chain): 0.845 (measured 0.902, giving 6.6e-9 — consistent). Measured rho so far: 0.90-0.91 (exact chain), 0.93-0.95 (Gaussian closure), both far below 0.99. The paper's analogue is that the unexplained part (1-rho^2) must be o(1) relative to the error being corrected, as every loss there is O(delta_n eps) relative to eps.
mechanisms.where: REPORT.md Sec. 2 (two-tier and dropped-window MSEs), sec_measure.tex lines 39-52; arithmetic in this analysis
mechanisms.status: PROVED (arithmetic; the (1-rho^2) floor is exact for a single scalar a; with the derived a = 1/(d+1) instead of a fitted one the residual is >= this floor). The rho of short-memory chains is the pending measurement (#13), so whether the route is open is OPEN.
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: F7 (window-1 error 53-64% collective vs exact chain's 0.2-5%) means the short chain's defect has a different, more coherent structure; the route survives only if its delta captures the collective part with rho ~ 0.99+, otherwise the (1-rho^2) floor (7e-7 at window 1-2) is 70x above target. The paper's methodology says: measure rho (the relative unexplained fraction) before investing in cheaper delta computations; absolute accuracy of delta is secondary to it (M7: 20% suffices once rho is high enough).

caveats: (1) The Gram-spectrum check (M8) is at n <= 96, L = 4, for the Gaussian closure with fresh He-random weights, not for the organisers' kappa3 chain, not at n = 1024, not on the official weights; the trends (sum|lambda|/|tr Q| and the Hutchinson ratio growing with n, spectrum flattening) are from three widths with two seeds and should be re-measured on the real chain before being quoted as a law. The claim 'Hutchinson on tr Q costs ~1e3 probes at n = 1024' extrapolates the ratio 5 at n = 96 and may be off by a factor 2-4. (2) The numerical verification of the secular identity is in float64 on Gaussian matrices; the paper's content is the subgaussian/discrete case (LCD, arithmetic quasirandomness), which is not testable by a 50x51 sample; the forced-event experiment fixes <v,X> deterministically rather than conditioning on it, which is the right geometry (the event depends on X only through its projections) but not a sample of the conditional law. (3) The truncation shares at n = 1000 (ell = 3 gives 91-94%) are one sample each; the paper's bound (log n)^{-1/8} is asymptotic and crude. (4) The correspondences 'kernel vector v <-> realisation-specific zero-mean bulk pairing', 'Lindeberg third-order term <-> kappa3 chain', 'E* <-> typicality of weights' are analogies used to organise the question, not theorems; I have marked them as such. (5) The task's figure |delta|/|e| ~ 7e-4 does not match the notes (6.6e-4 absolute rms vs |e| ~ 0.4 gives 1.6e-3); the budget conclusions do not depend on which normalisation is meant. (6) The (1-rho^2) floor assumes a single scalar correction constant; a per-layer or per-neuron a would lower the floor but is then a fitted object against F3's 'not learnable from local features'. (7) Nothing in the paper addresses cost; its truncation to sqrt(log n) directions is a probabilistic simplification, not an algorithm, and its relevance to the 0.1 B floor is only through the structural question (positive, decaying spectrum or not), which the measurements answer negatively for both delta and the memory. (8) The paper file was read fully from line 1 to 1250 and Appendix C; Appendices A-B were skimmed (flatness and negative-correlation lemmas), not verified.
